title: Getting the Buddy Rich job through Jimmy Mosher
summary: Mosher got him the Buddy Rich gig; he left school in days and first played lead book for Sinatra.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay so I went back to Berklee. Jimmy Mosher was the alto player who had just gotten off the summer tour with Buddy Rich. He did the “Away We Go” Jackie Gleason special, but he came back to Berklee to teach. So they put me in his ensemble, and I was in for about two weeks. On the second week we all go to a bar afterwards on a Friday night rehearsal — me, Lynn Bivvy — well Lynn had left already. And Lynn had gone on the

road — Lynn Biviano, the trumpet player. And he was out with Woody Herman. And so Jimmy Mosher was hanging out with Johnny in the bar and he said, “You know you’ve been in school too long.” He said, “You should go out on the road.” And we’re all drinking. And he said, “There’s a job opening with Buddy Rich. I’m going to make a call and get you the gig.” This was while we’re all drinking on Friday. So Monday morning comes around and I see Jimmy Mosher and I say, “Okay where’s that gig with Buddy Rich?” He said, “Quit all your classes and leave for New York, you start Thursday.” So I said oh my God. And I was in the recording band with Herb — I had to go tell Herb Pomeroy I was leaving school. I had to fly home and get a suitcase and I’d never flown before. I had to go back to Rochester. I had to fly to New York, and Ernie Watts, Ernie and I were already in an ensemble the year before with Charlie Mariano, but Ernie had taken the gig with Buddy Rich playing lead alto. And Charlie Owens, who was in Berklee also had taken the second alto gig. So when Jimmy Mosher got me the gig Ernie knew who I was, cause we had worked together. So I went to New York and I rehearsed for a week with the band without playing. We were working The Riverboat and I went down every night and caught the band so I could see what was going on. Last night Bobby Keller was the saxophone player, he came up to me and handed me the bag of suits, because there was a suit and a tuxedo. He says, “You got it.” Sunday morning we flew to Minneapolis/St. Paul. The first night, Frank Sinatra. At first, I get off the bus and Jay Corre, who was the tenor player, missed the plane, so I had to play the lead book, which I had never seen. I had only been rehearsing the fourth book. Now I’m stuck playing “West Side Story” and then backing Sinatra. A test of fire.
No. The thing is, both of my gigs, when I went with Elvin it was the same thing. No preparation just like bang, just jump in there and had to do it.
